pages.title: A1.1 Computer Hardware & Operation | IB Computer Science
pages.description: CPU components, registers, buses, memory hierarchy, and the fetch–decode–execute cycle (with HL pipelining).

pages.title: A1.2 Data Representation & Logic | IB Computer Science
pages.description: How computers represent numbers, text, images, and sound in binary — plus logic gates, truth tables, and HL Karnaugh maps.

pages.title: A1.3 Operating Systems & Control Systems | IB Computer Science
pages.description: The OS as resource manager: scheduling, memory, files, devices, interrupts — plus HL control systems and deadlock.

pages.title: A1.4 Translation (HL) | IB Computer Science
pages.description: HL: interpreters, compilers, bytecode and JIT — and how translation choices affect speed, portability, and error detection.

pages.title: A1 Computer Fundamentals - SGS Computer Science
pages.description: IB Computer Science Topic A1: Computer fundamentals. Interactive learning apps and revision resources.

pages.title: A2.1 Network Fundamentals | IB Computer Science
pages.description: Network types (PAN/LAN/WAN/VPN), bandwidth vs latency, and modern infrastructure (distributed systems, edge computing, 5G).

pages.title: A2.2 Network Architecture | IB Computer Science
pages.description: Network hardware roles (modem, router, switch, gateway) and architectural models (client–server vs peer-to-peer).

pages.title: A2.3 Data Transmission | IB Computer Science
pages.description: HL depth: TCP/IP layers, encapsulation, TCP vs UDP, packet switching, checksums, subnetting/CIDR, and NAT.

pages.title: A2.4 Network Security | IB Computer Science
pages.description: HL depth: common vulnerabilities (DDoS, SQL injection, MitM) and security mechanisms (encryption, certificates, Diffie–Hellman, firewalls).

pages.title: A2 Networks - SGS Computer Science
pages.description: IB Computer Science Topic A2: Networks. Interactive learning apps and revision resources.

pages.title: A3.1 Database Fundamentals | IB Computer Science
pages.description: Databases vs files, the relational model, keys, referential integrity, relationship types, and pros/cons of relational databases.

pages.title: A3.2 Database Design | IB Computer Science
pages.description: Schemas, ERDs, data types, table construction, normalization (to 3NF), and when denormalization is useful.

pages.title: A3.3 Database Programming | IB Computer Science
pages.description: SQL language types, joins, updating data, and HL extensions: aggregate functions, views, and transactions.

pages.title: A3.4 Alternative Databases & Data Warehouses (HL) | IB Computer Science
pages.description: HL: NoSQL database types, data warehouses, OLAP and data mining, and features of distributed databases.

pages.description: HL: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement and evolutionary approaches; neural networks and CNNs; hyperparameter tuning and model selection.
